units.translation: to endure, to remain: on which meaning see Thes. vol. 2 p. 1297.
But the faithless counsels of Laius endured.
to destroy utterly
to destroy utterly
The constant interpretation of this verb is διαφθείρειν [to destroy] in the glosses of grammarians collected in Thes. vol. 2 p. 1299.
so that they might not be utterly destroyed and go to Hades.
to destroy

to shout down, to drown with noise
Somewhat differently concerning that which someone casts in by shouting
which the scholiast explains as διὰ τοῦ θορύβου ἐμβεβλήκατε [you have cast in through the uproar].
shouting down: driving away.
you shouted down the lifeless cowardice,
you have cast in through the uproar
flowing apart, melting away
flowing apart, so that it flows apart.
Doric form διαρρύδαν [flowing apart]
where Lobeck corrected the accent which is in M διαρρυδάν [flowing apart].
the avenging murder is fixed, not flowing apart,
flowing apart

to divide, to distribute

Hesychius explains διάρτασον [divide!] by διάστειλον [separate!]. Therefore Aeschylus seems to have spoken of a herald carrying out his orders accurately. A similar verb is διαρτίζω [to arrange], on which see Thes. vol. 2 p. 1305.
ἄρταμος [butcher]: the cook – from διαρτάσαι [to divide], which is to divide or to fit together. Aeschylus (fr. 333) “So much, herald, divide from me.”
divide!
separate!
to arrange

to cut to pieces, to tear apart.
The noun derived from this, διαρταμή [cutting up], some would restore for διατομαῖς [cuttings]
on which see under the word διόσδοτος [god-given].
he will tear apart the great rag of the body.

to arrange in order, to set in rows
to arrange in order, to set in rows.

Hesychius: διεστοιχίζετο [was arranged in rows]: διετίθετο ἐν στοίχῳ καὶ τάξει [was placed in row and order], διήρει [divided], from those who lead the flocks into the pens and separate from the pasture each one's own.
and he was arranging the beginning in rows.
was arranged in rows: was placed in row and order, divided, from those who lead the flocks into the pens and separate from the pasture each one's own
